# AI NETRA — Data sources and provenance

| Provider | Dataset / acquisition | Used for | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenStreetMap contributors | Overpass API (`https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter`) | Building footprints and Musi mapped water geometry | Crowdsourced, not survey-verified; ODbL attribution required |
| Google Research | Google Open Buildings 2.5D temporal dataset via Earth Engine (`GOOGLE/Research/open-buildings-temporal/v1`) | 2023 model-estimated building heights | Not field-measured; 0 and suspiciously low values require special handling |
| Telangana Government TGRAC | ArcGIS REST layer `GHMCNalas_Folder/GHMCNalas_vul/MapServer/1` | 23 named mapped waterlogging points | Original folder `MAJOR WATER LOGGING PLACES.kmz/Water logging`; no event dates, flood depths, or inundation boundaries |
| ISRO NRSC Bhuvan | Disaster portal investigated | Potential historical flood information | Portal map controls did not work during investigation; **not integrated** |

## Source references
- OpenStreetMap: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
- Google Earth Engine catalog: https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/GOOGLE_Research_open-buildings-temporal_v1
- TGRAC ArcGIS REST: https://tgrac.telangana.gov.in/arcgis/rest/services/GHMCNalas_Folder/GHMCNalas_vul/MapServer/1
- NRSC Bhuvan flood portal: https://bhuvan-app1.nrsc.gov.in/disaster/usrtasks/flood/flood.php

## Data handling
Preserve original downloads as `*_raw_*`. Store derived calculations in separate versioned files. Preserve the provider, geometry type, transformation method, retrieval date where known, source timestamps where available, and validation status. The source provider's exact licensing and reuse terms should be verified before publication.

**Critical distinction:** TGRAC's layer is named *Inundation Areas*, but its retrieved data consists of named **waterlogging points**, not inundation polygons; the data does not establish historical flooding of particular buildings.

## Sentinel-1 Historical Radar Change Experiment — October 2020

### Data source
- Provider: European Space Agency / Copernicus
- Processing platform: Google Earth Engine
- Dataset: COPERNICUS/S1_GRD
- Polarization: VV
- Acquisition mode: IW
- Orbit direction: DESCENDING
- Relative orbit number: 165
- Pilot coverage: 100% for all three observations

### Acquisition dates
- 2020-09-27 00:38 UTC
- 2020-10-09 00:38 UTC
- 2020-10-21 00:38 UTC

### Processing
- Applied a 30-metre circular focal median filter.
- Calculated post-minus-pre radar backscatter differences in dB.
- Evaluated changes at 10-metre nominal analysis scale.
- Used thresholds of +3 dB and -3 dB.

### Results

| Category | Control (%) | Event (%) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Increase above +3 dB | 0.21 | 50.16 |
| Decrease below -3 dB | 16.84 | 0.97 |
| Moderate change | 82.95 | 48.87 |

### Interpretation
The event comparison exhibits substantially more positive
radar-backscatter changes than the control comparison.

These differences do not independently establish flooding.

### Limitations
- Only three satellite acquisitions were examined.
- The two comparison periods share the October 9 observation.
- The October 21 observation may miss peak inundation.
- Radar changes can result from non-flooding factors.
- Urban radar scattering complicates flood identification.
- No ground-truth inundation dataset has been used.
- No validated flood mask has been produced.
- No building-level historical flood exposure is confirmed.

### Current evidence status
Historical satellite radar-change evidence — unverified
for inundation classification.


## JRC Global Surface Water Validation — November 2026

### Dataset
- Provider: Joint Research Centre / Google Earth Engine
- Dataset: JRC/GSW1_4/GlobalSurfaceWater
- Nominal resolution: 30 metres
- Pilot: Moosarambagh–Musi River corridor

### Experimental Results

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---:|
| Valid occurrence samples | 2 |
| Missing occurrence weighted total | 8263.44 |
| Frequent water (>=90%) | 0 |
| Occasional water (1–89%) | 0.024 |
| Valid zero occurrence | 0 |
| Historical water extent samples | 2 |

### Interpretation

The occurrence-band analysis provides insufficient
valid reference information for the current pilot.

Reported raster reductions may contain fractional
weighted values and should not be interpreted as
exact counts of independent pixels.

Masked occurrence pixels must not be interpreted
as dry land.

### Decision

Do not use the current JRC occurrence analysis
to validate Sentinel-1 flood classifications.

Do not classify buildings as flooded using these results.

### Status

Investigated — insufficient usable reference data
under the current analysis configuration.


## Sentinel-1 Dual-Polarization Analysis — October 2020

### Dataset
- Google Earth Engine: COPERNICUS/S1_GRD
- Satellite: Sentinel-1
- Polarizations: VV and VH
- Instrument mode: IW
- Orbit: Descending
- Relative orbit: 165
- Pilot: Moosarambagh–Musi River corridor

### Acquisition Dates
- 2020-09-27
- 2020-10-09
- 2020-10-21

### Processing
- 30-metre focal median filtering.
- Post-minus-pre backscatter comparison in dB.
- Positive-change threshold: > +3 dB.
- Dual-polarization overlap: VV > +3 dB AND VH > +3 dB.
- Analysis scale: 10 metres.

### Results

| Measurement | Control (%) | Event (%) |
|---|---:|---:|
| VV increase > +3 dB | 0.21 | 50.16 |
| VH increase > +3 dB | 0.20 | 23.25 |
| VV and VH overlap > +3 dB | 0.00 | 14.29 |

### Interpretation

The event-period comparison contains substantially
more simultaneous positive VV/VH radar changes than
the preceding control comparison.

The overlap is a radar-change indicator, not a
validated inundation classification.

### Limitations
- Only one pre-event control interval was analyzed.
- Control and event comparisons share the October 9 image.
- The October 21 image may not represent peak flooding.
- No verified ground-truth flood polygons were used.
- The +3 dB threshold has not been independently validated.
- Urban radar-scattering effects remain unresolved.
- No building-level flood exposure has been established.

### Evidence Status

Historical dual-polarization radar-change evidence:
UNVERIFIED FOR FLOOD DETECTION.
